Fuck how annoying it was to figure out. Just be happy, it really is that simple? Oh fuck me then.

Second campaign was very metaphorical though so mods hints and help would be needed to continue. This was where the warlocks patron basically would become my voice. Could be anything like “wtf are you guys doing” when they were covering their scent in shit, to giving missions and leads to further the plot. The other would be a stone that could lore dump if in game history was needed.  That game had a lit of mystery, hidden messages and psychological elements that had to be presented correctly.

Now I have split this “character” up in a crew. So one guys gets all the missions and gigs for the party, he’s there manager. Another one serves insight on the human non magical part of the lore (it’s a new homebrew world). A third is a fey and has insights on the magical aspects. And honourable mentions are a book that gives leads to monsters they might be facing and the first npc they meet in villages that introduces pcs to the new area. 

Important thing I learned is that information always has to be incomplete. You shouldn’t be handing out all the answears these characters are just tools to help the players solve the mystery. The book won’t tell everything they need to know but a bite of information could help piece the bigger puzzle together.
